title: Round battery percentage to match the bar without tripping hold early
head: 9aa09a0b5f27
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A decimal-comma UPower locale still truncates the fractional percentage and disagrees with the bar
leads.consequence: UPower uses the caller's locale for %g. With de_DE.utf8 and 79.5% on the bus, its CLI prints 79,5%; this script's awk converts that token to 79, displays 79%, while Quickshell's D-Bus percentage renders 80%. The new tests force C-style decimal input and do not check this locale. Exit is 0; notification and power-panel hero show the wrong percentage at every refresh. This already affected the old truncation, but the PR's claimed bar alignment is not attained for such users. Parse the locale-aware CLI value with a matching parser or consume the numerical D-Bus property, and add a non-C fixture.
leads.triage: corroborated; Opus finding 6 (decimal-comma locale); published as pre-existing note

leads.summary: Combining #10076's live kernel percentage with this PR retains stale UPower data for hold decisions
leads.consequence: #10076 explicitly changes the printed percentage and the bar's data source to live sysfs charge/energy, to handle stale UPower values, but this PR's raw_percentage continues to come from UPower. In the file-level merged script, an 80% live pack with UPower stuck at 20%, 80% charge cap, 0.1W and AC on prints percentage 80%, state charging, not holding. The head's 79.5/80 regression tests still pass and miss this case. Align the raw hold comparison with whichever percentage source wins (kernel when valid). #10076 currently has a separate Service.qml patch reject and GitHub reports CONFLICTING; this consequence applies if its battery-status hunk is retained when conflicts are resolved.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_opus_followup; #10076 interaction; neutral SendMessage, answer opus/followup-10076.md, run-verified; published as own section

leads.summary: #7915's pending-charge band guard compares this PR's rounded display value rather than its raw value
leads.consequence: The merged script reports state=holding when pending-charge is 74.5% and the configured charge band is 75-80%, despite the raw charge being below the start. #7915's panel independently checks the unrounded D-Bus fraction against the band and will not call the same state a hold. Both PRs' battery and power tests pass because #7915 only tries integers 0,78,90. Use raw_percentage for both ends of #7915's new band predicate, and exercise a half-percent below the start. The head alone already calls all pending-charge a hold; the break here is #7915's new gate not delivering its documented improvement when these changes coexist.

leads.summary: The open Snapdragon battery lookup PR #13029 merges its code but its fractional-percentage fixture fails
leads.consequence: #13029 stubs UPower percentage 74.8351% and asserts 'percentage\t74%', intentionally checking the non-BAT system battery. After both branches merge, this PR's new display rounding produces 75%, so the default test/shell suite exits at that assertion before checking state/cycles or later files. Change the other PR's expected output to 75% when rebasing, preserving its lookup and peripheral checks.

leads.summary: The UPower CLI has already rounded away bits of the 'raw' value before the new comparison
leads.consequence: UPower's %g formats only six significant digits while the bar uses its numeric D-Bus double. A possible 79.49999% on the bus prints as '79.5%' in upower -i, so the script displays 80% while the bar rounds to 79%; 79.99999% prints as 80%, so the new raw comparison can mark an 80% charging hold before the actual fraction reaches 80. Exit is 0, and the power notice/shell output continues to misrepresent the value on successive reads. The latter early hold also existed with the old integer comparison, but this PR's claim that it now compares the unrounded percentage is false for this representable upstream input. Query D-Bus numeric Percentage directly if truly raw comparisons are required.
leads.triage: dropped; %g six-digit precision; verified printf %g 79.99999 -> 80, but pre-existing, ~1e-5 wide; Opus bar-precision note kept in test scope only

leads.summary: Added threshold fixtures cannot catch a regression to integer comparison in fully-charged branch
leads.consequence: Both added fixtures use state=charging. Restoring the old '(( percentage < 99 ))' solely in the fully-charged branch makes every new test pass. For UPower's permitted fully-charged 98.5% value the mutant no longer flags the hold because its display percentage is 99%, while the intended raw comparison would. Add a fully-charged, 98.5% fixture under AC with a threshold and assert state holding, plus 99.0% as the non-hold boundary. This is a coverage gap, not a claim that the shipped branch is broken.
leads.triage: corroborated; Opus finding 4 (fully-charged test gap); published as Optional test improvement

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change does what it describes. The panel percentage now rounds half-up (`printf "%d", p + 0.5`), which equals the bar's `Math.round` (`shell/plugins/panels/power/Panel.qml:281`) for a single battery. The charge-hold checks give the same result as before in every tested case: with whole-number thresholds and values of 0 or more, `int(p) >= t` equals `p >= t`, and `int(p) < 99` equals `p < 99`. Across 23 synthetic `upower -i` reports, the `state` output was identical between base and head. The new test passes on the head and fails on the base at the display assertion. Its hold assertion also fails for a naive "round everywhere" variant, so it guards the design.

The main point is how the redefined `percentage` interacts with other open PRs.

### Open PRs that compare `percentage` would compare the rounded value

After this PR, `percentage` holds the rounded display value, and the two existing percentage-based hold checks (fully-charged and idle-charging) read `raw_percentage`. Two open PRs add new `percentage` comparisons to the hold block: #7915 (`percentage >= threshold_start && percentage <= threshold_end`) and #12115 (`percentage >= threshold_floor`). The `bin/omarchy-battery-status` changes of each merge with this PR's version without a textual conflict, and the new checks from those PRs then use the rounded value.

Synthetic run, pending-charge on AC with a 75-80% limit:

| UPower reading | Other PR alone | Combined with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 74.6% | #12115: `pending-charge` ("Not charging") | `holding` ("Holding at 75-80%") |
| 74.6% | #7915: `pending-charge` | `holding` |
| 80.6% | #7915: `holding` | `pending-charge` |

The first row is the early hold this PR sets out to prevent.

**Impact:** once combined, the new checks from those PRs compare the rounded value, and the scripts merge without any conflict to flag it. The combined battery-status tests of this PR and #7915 still pass.

**Suggested change:** keep `percentage` as the truncated value used for comparisons and add a separate display variable. Truncated `>=` and `<` comparisons against whole-number thresholds are already exact, so the existing hold block then needs no change and no extra `awk` calls:

```bash
percentage=$(awk '/percentage/ { print int($2); exit }' <<<"$battery_info")
display_percentage=$(awk '/percentage/ { printf "%d", $2 + 0.5; exit }' <<<"$battery_info")
```

Then use `${display_percentage}%` in the `--shell` `percentage` line and the three `Battery ...%` lines. In a synthetic run this variant passes the PR's test and gives the same output as the head for 13 of 14 reports in both modes. The one difference is a report with no percentage line, where it prints `%` as the base did, instead of the head's `0%`.

### #10076 would split the display and hold sources

#10076, which currently conflicts with `quattro`, reassigns `percentage` from sysfs in its battery-status change, but not `raw_percentage`. Combined with this PR, the printed value and the hold checks then read different sources. In a synthetic run with UPower stuck at 10.6% and sysfs at 99.37% `Full`, on AC with an 80% limit, the combination prints `Battery 99%  ·  Holding at 80%`, while #10076 alone reports `fully-charged`.

**Impact:** after both land, a machine where UPower and sysfs disagree can show a hold that matches neither the printed percentage nor either PR's intent. The alternative in the previous section does not cover this case, because it keeps printing UPower's value.

**Suggested change:** when #10076 is rebased onto this PR, its sysfs blocks need to set both the comparison value (`raw_percentage`, unrounded) and the display value (`percentage`).

### Related test in #13029

#13029 adds a test whose stub reports `74.8351%` and expects `percentage\t74%`. Its changes merge with this PR without conflict, but the combined test fails (`not ok - battery status finds a non-BAT system battery`, output `75%`). Whichever PR lands second needs the expectation changed to `75%`, or a stub value with a fraction below .5 (for example `74.3%`).

**Description accuracy:** the PR body says that with truncation "79.5% could look like an 80% hold". The old code truncated 79.5 to 79, and `79 >= 80` is false, so it never held early. The raw comparisons keep the new rounding out of the hold checks, which is what the code comment in the diff says. Rewording the body or commit message would avoid it being read as a hold-logic fix.

**Optional test improvement:** the fully-charged branch (`bin/omarchy-battery-status:97`) is not covered. A variant that compares the rounded value there, `(( percentage < 99 ))`, passes all the new tests. This block, added after the second new block, passes on the head and fails on that variant:

```bash
sed -i 's/state:                charging/state:                fully-charged/; s/percentage:           80.0%/percentage:           98.6%/' "$hold_dir/bin/upower"
full_output=$(OMARCHY_POWER_SUPPLY_PATH="$hold_dir/power" PATH="$hold_dir/bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-battery-status" --shell)
grep -Fx $'percentage\t99%' <<<"$full_output" >/dev/null || fail "98.6% displays as 99%" "$full_output"
grep -Fx $'state\tholding' <<<"$full_output" >/dev/null || fail "fully-charged below 99% is holding" "$full_output"
pass "battery status keeps a fully-charged pack below 99% holding"
```

**Decimal-comma locales (pre-existing):** `upower` calls `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` and prints the percentage with `%g`, so under a locale such as `de_DE` it prints `79,5%` (from UPower source). `awk` reads that as `79`, so those users still see a truncated value that can differ from the bar. Time parsing is affected the same way, and so is the rate when the script falls back to UPower's `energy-rate` (no sysfs power or current readings). A follow-up using `battery_info=$(LC_ALL=C upower -i "$battery")` would cover all three.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the head, the base and current `quattro` versions (both changed files are unchanged on `quattro`), the power panel and bar consumers, UPower v1.91.4 and Quickshell v0.3.1. The PR's tests, base/head comparisons, test variants and merges with open PRs ran in an isolated sandbox with a stubbed `upower` and synthetic power-supply trees. No real battery, UPower daemon or desktop was used. Decimal-comma UPower output is taken from source, not run. On most non-MacBook laptops UPower reports the kernel's whole-number `capacity`, so the display change is mostly visible where UPower computes a fractional percentage. Rare floating-point edge cases, such as a reading of exactly 14.5%, can still differ from the bar by 1%.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
